assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Removing @pytest.mark.timeout(3840) reverts the test to the 300 s global bound and it fails with Failed: Timeout (>300.0s) instead of reaching its own identity assertions; the marker-removed negative control at head reproduces exactly this.
Removing @pytest.mark.timeout(3840) reverts the compiled-slice test to the 300 s global bound; its H200 wall is 25.01 s so on CPU it would only trip on a genuine hang, guarded by the bound itself.

assertion_note: the diff adds no assertions; the two decorators are the guard

findings.text: follow-on: the brief asks N to be 1.5x each test's own CPU wall, but only the combined two-test CPU wall (2532.78 s, cpu-measurement-1290974.log) was measured, so the compiled-slice test carries 3840 s where max(its own CPU wall, 25.01 s H200) x 1.5 would be far tighter; a genuine hang in that test surfaces only after 64 minutes on the CPU lane. The bound is above the measured wall so it never under-bounds, and the deviation is disclosed in the commit body and the evidence fragment.
